function: Complex-valued CNN detector recovering M-ary symbols (then antenna and polarization indices through minimum Euclidean distance) for RIS-assisted dual-polarized generalized spatial modulation (p. 4).
system: Reflecting passive RIS with N = 16 dual-polarized elements; Nt = Nr = 4 dual-polarized antennas, M = 4; frequency band not stated (p. 2, p. 4).
method: Complex-valued CNN (2 conv layers 256 and 128 filters, cReLU, complex FC with softmax), supervised, cross-entropy, Nadam, 50 epochs, 10^6 samples (p. 4, Table I).
data_channel: Own simulator: dual-polarized Rician (K = 5) Tx-RIS and Rayleigh RIS-Rx links with XPD, XPI, correlation; 10^6 random samples at 10 dB; no public dataset (p. 2-4).
test_conditions: Training: 10^6 samples at 10 dB SNR, 70% training and 30% validation/testing; testing: SNR 0-22 dB, mu = 0.6/0.8, perfect and imperfect CSI, N = 8/16/32 (p. 4-5).
baselines: Non-learned: ML, B-ZF, MOB-MMSE detectors; scheme baseline RIS-UPGSM. No earlier learned detector compared (p. 4-5).
metrics: BER versus SNR, SE in bpcu, SNR gain at fixed BER, theoretical complexity, running time (p. 4-5).
complexity: CVCNN O(f1 f2 K) versus ML, B-ZF and MOB-MMSE orders in Table II; running time in Fig. 5(b) (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 2: "is a Rician fading channel as in [4]"; p. 3: G "also follows Rayleigh fading"; custom statistical model with XPD, XPI and correlations, no standardized or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 4: "The training SNR is 10dB" and "70% of the datasets is reserved for training and the remaining 30% acts as validation and testing"; sweeps of SNR, CSI error, mu and N (Figs. 3-6) are not stated as tests of a model trained elsewhere.
q3_support: p. 4: "evaluated by the comparison with the ML detector, the ZF detector and the MMSE detector"; no earlier learned detector is compared in the results, DL detectors [11]-[14] appear only in the introduction (p. 1).
q4_support: p. 5: "the computational complexity of the CVCNN detector can be shown in Table II as O(f1 f2 K )"; Fig. 5(b) reports running time.
q5_support: p. 4: "We select a random generated dataset" (10^6 samples, Table I); simulations "accomplished by Tensorflow in Python"; no code or data link or DOI, and no public dataset.
notes: Area 1: the CVCNN predicts the transmitted symbols and the antenna and polarization indices follow by minimum Euclidean distance (p. 4), so BER detection is the function. The RIS is passive and its phase design is out of scope (p. 3, footnote 1), so area 3 does not apply. In Fig. 5(b) the CVCNN running time, read from the bars, is below ML and close to ZF and MMSE (p. 5).
